items.stem: What is the main purpose of market segmentation?

options.text: To group customers with similar needs so you can target and serve them better
options.rationale: Correct: segmentation enables focused targeting and relevant messaging.

options.text: To increase the total number of products
options.rationale: Segmentation is about customers, not product count.

options.text: To lower the price for everyone
options.rationale: It informs strategy, not a blanket price cut.

items.explanation: Correct: segmentation enables focused targeting and relevant messaging.

items.stem: A brand's positioning is 'premium, hand-crafted quality'. Which TWO marketing-mix choices are consistent with it? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A price at the higher end of the category
options.rationale: Correct: premium pricing reinforces the quality positioning.
Correct: selective placement signals exclusivity and quality.

options.text: Deep permanent discounting in bulk outlets
options.rationale: Heavy discounting undermines a premium position.

options.text: Messaging focused only on being the cheapest
options.rationale: A cheapest-price message contradicts premium positioning.

items.explanation: Correct: premium pricing and selective distribution fit the positioning.

items.stem: A campaign reports millions of impressions but no change in sales or sign-ups. What is the main issue?

options.text: Measuring a vanity metric rather than an outcome tied to business goals
options.rationale: Correct: impressions alone do not show business impact.

options.text: The campaign reached too few people
options.rationale: Reach was high; impact was not measured meaningfully.
Positioning matters, but the issue here is the metric chosen.

options.text: The funnel has too many stages
options.rationale: Funnel length is not the problem described.
